svg.title: Figure 2-2: SF-02 by the rear bumper, reversing at the crawl limit: contact to standstill against the edge's overtravel
svg.desc: Six boxes from contact through the edge, the monitoring unit and relay, the contactors, the coast and the standstill; a time axis to 0.6 s with both coast cases; a millimetre-scale ledger with the 7 mm fast-coast and 17 mm slow-coast stopping distances inside the 20 to 40 mm overtravel band; a floor strip with the robot reversing toward the dock over the blind 0.7 m path and a person behind it.

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Figure 2-2 SF-02 by the rear bumper, reversing at the crawl limit: contact to standstill against the edge's overtravel

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: §2 row SF-02 (bumper path): 20 + 50 + 20 = 90 ms against the 170 ms target; reverse at the crawl limit 0.05 m/s (DQ-018 A), CFG-001; the edge detects by contact, so there is no distance before it (§4.3).

svg.text: Distance ledger: the stopping distance after contact against the edge's overtravel

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: drawn to scale, 1 mm = 20 px; the edge must still be compressing when the robot stops, or the force rises to the wheel torque

svg.text: d_s = v·t_r + v²/2a = 0.05 × 0.09 + 0.05²/(2 × 0.5) = 7 mm on the fast coast, 17 mm on the slow one (a = 0.1): inside the 20 to 40 mm overtravel of a Mayser SL/BK class edge (TBC).

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Above about 0.1 m/s the slow-coast stop (59 mm) outruns the overtravel: the speed monitor's direction-and-speed rule (SR-03.02) keeps the bumper adequate; the reverse limit is a safety parameter (§4.3).

svg.text: Drawn to WP-S-04 v0.2 planning values (t_r 0.09 s, a = 0.5 and 0.1 m/s² unmeasured). A loop diagram shows the arithmetic of a stop; it does not show that a measure works.
